title: What a person did with what a kind of help produced: the outcome's contract, capture and store side
request: The owner: do 36.2 next, so the tracks that are not prediction leave training data with an outcome label.
spec: PHASE12_TRAINING_DATA_PLAN.md 36.2: a non-prediction track ends with something a person can judge and the person's verdict; recorded as events and as labels of request.intent and the routing decision (person gold, rules silver); m2 gets the routing with its outcome, m4 each conversation with thinking labelled by its outcome. The Home session owns draft/; this package adds the store side and the contract, agreed with it first.
plan: Map what Home records today and what the store builds
Agree the contract with the Home session before any change
Test first, then the contract, the event, the capture and the store side

decisions.decision: Read the verdict from the conversation's ordered action names
decisions.why: the Home session's calls give an action list; thumbs alone miss saving, taking a table, or saying no to a step

decisions.decision: Fold the Home session's tested rule into dclab_core instead of writing a second rule
decisions.why: one rule read by Home, the ledger capture and the store

decisions.decision: Only a person's kept or changed labels the route taken
decisions.why: a refusal says the result was poor, not that the kind of help was wrong; guessing a right answer from it would teach the routing model a lie

decisions.decision: A later non-confirming verdict supersedes the earlier label with an empty one
decisions.why: Home records on every change; a keep then an unsave must leave no confirmed route

decisions.decision: The store picks labels only among those no later label supersedes
decisions.why: the ledger's own rule; without it a retraction would be ignored

decisions.decision: A dashboard refresh is no verdict; a thumb is
decisions.why: a refresh only recomputes the tiles, maybe because the numbers look wrong

change: dclab_core/track_outcome.py; ExperienceEvent v16 track.outcome (schemas, baseline, adapters, dclab-core 0.135.0); dclab_rnd/ledger/capture.py track_outcome; store/sets/llm.py check.outcome; store/sets/decisions.py current labels only; store/coverage.py; CORE_INTEGRATION.md; PHASE12 status; tests.

findings.defect: The event's new version broke tests and a generated file elsewhere
findings.scenario: four test files and the data catalog still said version 15
findings.cause: the version is pinned in several places outside the package's own files
findings.fix: the pins moved to version 16 and the catalog was rebuilt by its command

findings.defect: A keep followed by a refusal left a confirmed route
findings.scenario: the person saves an answer, then unsaves it; the routing model would learn the route as right
findings.cause: labels were written on a keep and never taken back
findings.fix: a later verdict that does not confirm supersedes the function's own label with an empty one; the store reads only labels no later label supersedes

findings.defect: A verdict read by the rules could become a confirmed label
findings.scenario: an outcome kept by the rules would have written a measured label, counted as gold
findings.cause: the contract did not tie who decided to the verdict
findings.fix: the contract refuses a kept, changed or refused verdict not decided by the person, and only the person's verdicts label

findings.defect: A result nobody judged recorded no event
findings.scenario: produced and never judged could not be counted
findings.cause: the function returned early on an open verdict
findings.fix: an open verdict is an event without a label

findings.defect: A dashboard refresh counted as kept
findings.scenario: a person refreshing because the numbers look wrong would be recorded as keeping the dashboard
findings.cause: refresh was in the decisive actions
findings.fix: refresh is no verdict; a thumb up or down on the reply is

findings.defect: A third session wrote a different design into the same files
findings.scenario: two designs interleaved in the store code and a shared test file was overwritten
findings.cause: two sessions picked the same package in one working tree
findings.fix: the other session removed its edits; the agreed design stands; tests moved to their own file

outcome: The outcome of a non-prediction track now has a contract, an event, ledger labels and a store field: a person's kept or changed confirms the route taken, a later refusal takes it back, and each Home conversation in m4 carries its verdict. No verdict is recorded yet: Home's calls are the Home session's next step.
lessons: Agree a shared contract with the session that owns the calling code before writing it.
Labels written on every change need a way back: supersede, never edit.
Tie who decided to the verdict in the contract, so a rule's reading can never become gold.
When a version is pinned in many files, search the whole repository before committing.
risks: Refused and asked again reach m4 only, not m2: an outcome field on m2 examples is a later contract change.
One verdict per conversation: earlier results in a long conversation lose theirs.
